title: Operationalising Weaker Faithfulness: Recovery, Ambiguity and Computational Limits
abstract: arXiv:2610.31724v1 Announce Type: cross  Abstract: Variables can predict an outcome jointly while each is individually independent of it, causing structure learners to discard informative links. We investigate how to operationalise weaker faithfulness through two approaches: selective protection in an adjacency learner and explicit retention of alternative directed graph explanations. Matched experiments show that changes at both an early candidate-removal stage and later pruning can be necessary. In noisy XOR with a descendant (N = 10,000, 20 matched samples), combining reactivation and protection raises complete parent-pair recovery from 0/20 for either change alone to 20/20, while adding false edges. A confirmation study shows that the family estimator can preserve explanations lost by orienting the protected learner's selected skeleton: in one weaker signal XOR condition (N = 10,000) it retains the entire reference family in 48/50 samples, compared with 0/50 for the skeleton adapte

translated_title: 操作化较弱忠实性：恢复、歧义与计算极限
translated_abstract: 变量可以联合预测某个结果，而每个变量单独却与该结果相互独立，这会导致结构学习器丢弃含有信息量的关联。我们研究如何通过两种途径来操作化较弱忠实性：一是在邻接学习器中进行选择性保护，二是显式保留备选的有向图解释。匹配实验表明，早期候选移除阶段与后期剪枝阶段两处的改动都可能是必要的。在带后代节点的噪声XOR实验中（N=10,000，20个匹配样本），将重新激活与保护相结合，使完整父节点对的恢复率从单独采用任一改动时的0/20提升至20/20，但同时会引入假边。一项验证性研究显示，家族估计器能够保留因对受保护学习器所选骨架进行定向而丢失的解释：在一个较弱信号的XOR条件下（N=10,000），它在48/50个样本中保留了完整的参考解释家族，而骨架自适应[估计器]仅为0/50。
tldr: 本文提出两种操作化弱忠实性的策略——邻接学习中的选择性边保护与显式保留备选有向图解释（解释家族），使结构学习器能够恢复单独独立但联合预测结果的变量（如XOR）之间的联系，将完整父对恢复率从0/20提升至20/20，且家族估计器在48/50的样本中保留了全部备选解释。
en_tdlr: By combining selective edge protection in an adjacency learner with explicit retention of alternative directed-graph explanations, this work operationalises weaker faithfulness, recovering jointly-predictive-but-marginally-independent variable links (raising complete parent-pair recovery from 0/20 to 20/20) while a family estimator preserves the entire reference explanation family in 48/50 samples.
